lessons.title: Passive voice, conditionals 0-3, wish and if only
lessons.programRef: 1re — Anglais : passif, conditionnels, wish (à vérifier sur le texte officiel)
lessons.author: CastBridge (brouillon IA)
lessons.source: Rédaction originale ; textes, poèmes et exercices écrits pour CastBridge ; à relire par un enseignant
objectives: Former le passif à différents temps et l'employer à bon escient.
Distinguer les conditionnels de type 0, 1, 2 et 3.
Exprimer un regret ou un souhait avec wish et if only.
Éviter les erreurs fréquentes (will ou would après if).
reviewNotes: Programme exact (conditionnels exigibles, mixed conditionals, passif impersonnel, wish) à vérifier sur le texte officiel ; ici : types 0 à 3 et wish/if only comme demandé.
Norme : « If I were » (formel) / « If I was » (courant) : la forme à exiger en examen est à confirmer par l'enseignant.
Le vocabulaire grammatical (en français ou en anglais) et les formes d'écriture « were/was » peuvent varier selon le manuel.

blocks.title: La voix passive : forme
blocks.md:
**Forme** : **be** (au temps voulu) + **participe passé**. Le complément d'objet de la phrase active devient le sujet.
- present simple : *The letter **is written**.*
- past simple : *The letter **was written**.*
- present perfect : *The letter **has been written**.*
- future : *The letter **will be written**.*
- modal : *The letter **must be written**.*
- present continuous : *The letter **is being written**.*

blocks.title: Emploi du passif
blocks.md:
On emploie le passif quand l'**action** ou celui qui la **subit** compte plus que l'auteur, ou quand l'auteur est **inconnu** ou **évident**. L'agent est introduit par **by**, seulement s'il est important.

*Mr Ndi wrote the letter.* → *The letter was written **by Mr Ndi**.*
*Someone stole my bicycle.* → *My bicycle was stolen.*

Avec deux compléments : *She gave him a book.* → *He was given a book.* ou *A book was given to him.*
Tournures impersonnelles : *It is said that…, He is said to be rich.*

blocks.title: Les conditionnels (0 à 3)
blocks.md:
- **Type 0** (vérité générale) : *If you heat ice, it melts.*
- **Type 1** (futur possible) : *If it rains, we will stay at home.*
- **Type 2** (irréel du présent, improbable) : *If I had a car, I would drive to Kribi.* On écrit *If I were you…* pour donner un conseil.
- **Type 3** (irréel du passé) : *If I had studied, I would have passed.*

*Unless* = *if … not* : *Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.*

blocks.caption: Les quatre types de phrases conditionnelles.
blocks.alt: Un tableau à trois colonnes : Type, If-clause, Main clause ; quatre lignes : 0 avec present simple et present simple ; 1 avec present simple et will plus base verb ; 2 avec past simple et would plus base verb ; 3 avec past perfect et would have plus participe passé.

blocks.title: Wish et if only
blocks.md:
**Wish** et **if only** expriment un regret ou un souhait :
- **Présent** (regret sur une situation actuelle) : wish + **past simple** : *I wish I **had** a bicycle.* *If only I **were** taller.*
- **Passé** (regret sur le passé) : wish + **past perfect** : *I wish I **had studied** harder.*
- **Plainte, souhait de changement** : wish + **would** : *I wish it **would stop** raining.*

*If only* est plus **intense** que *I wish*.

blocks.title: Pièges pour francophones
blocks.md:
- **Pas de will après if** : *If it rains, we stay* ✓ ; *If it will rain* ✗.
- **Pas de would après if** : *If I had money, I would travel* ✓ ; *If I would have money* ✗.
- Le **participe passé** reste indispensable au passif : *The bridge was **built*** (et non *was build*).
- Le français « on a volé mon vélo » donne souvent le passif anglais : *My bicycle was stolen.*

blocks.title: Exemple 1 : de l'actif au passif
blocks.statement: Rewrite in the passive: (1) The teacher corrected the exercises. (2) People speak English in Buea. (3) They have built a new market.

steps.md: (1) Le complément « the exercises » devient sujet ; le verbe est au simple past : *The exercises **were corrected** by the teacher.*
(2) Present simple : *English **is spoken** in Buea.* (l'agent « people » est inutile).
(3) Present perfect : *A new market **has been built**.* On conserve le temps de l'actif : have built → has been built.

blocks.answer: (1) The exercises were corrected by the teacher. (2) English is spoken in Buea. (3) A new market has been built.

blocks.title: Exemple 2 : choisir le type de conditionnel
blocks.statement: Complete: (1) If it rains tomorrow, we (stay) at home. (2) If I (be) you, I would apologise. (3) If she (study) harder last year, she would have passed.

steps.md: (1) « If … rains » (présent) : conditionnel de **type 1** → *we **will stay** at home.*
(2) « would apologise » : **type 2** → *If I **were** you*, formule de conseil.
(3) « would have passed » : **type 3** → *If she **had studied** harder last year.*

blocks.title: Exemple 3 : exprimer un regret
blocks.statement: Say it with « wish » : (1) I don't have a phone. (2) I didn't learn English earlier. (3) It rains every day.

steps.md: (1) Regret présent : *I wish I **had** a phone.*
(2) Regret passé : *I wish I **had learnt** English earlier.*

blocks.answer: I wish I had a phone. / I wish I had learnt English earlier. / I wish it would stop raining.

blocks.title: Erreurs fréquentes
blocks.md:
- *If I will go…* ✗ → *If I go…* (type 1).
- *If I would have time…* ✗ → *If I had time, I would…*
- *I wish I would have a car* ✗ → *I wish I had a car*.
- Oublier **be** au passif : *The letter written by Paul* ✗.
- Employer **by** devant un agent inutile : *English is spoken by people* ✗ (inutile).

exercises.prompt: Match each conditional sentence with its type.
pairs: If you heat ice, it melts.
If it rains, we will stay at home.
If I had a car, I would drive to Kribi.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
I wish I had more time.
exercises.explanation: Le type dépend du temps de l'if-clause : présent → 0 ou 1 ; past simple → 2 ; past perfect → 3.
exercises.method: Regarder le temps de la proposition en if.

exercises.explanation: « Yesterday » exige un temps du passé : was/were + participe passé (were written).

exercises.prompt: True or false: « If I would have money, I would travel. » is correct.
exercises.explanation: Faux. Après « if » on n'emploie pas would : *If I had money, I would travel.*

exercises.prompt: I wish I ___ a bicycle. (I don't have one.)
exercises.explanation: Un regret sur une situation actuelle se dit avec wish + past simple : *I wish I had…*

exercises.prompt: Rewrite: (1) Someone has stolen my bag. → passive. (2) Unless you study, you will fail. → with « if ». (3) She didn't call me, so I was angry. → « If … » (type 3). (4) I don't live near the sea. → « I wish … ».
exercises.model: (1) **My bag has been stolen.** (2) **If you don't study, you will fail.** (3) **If she had called me, I wouldn't have been angry.** (4) **I wish I lived near the sea.**
rubric: Unless remplacé par if … not (1 point).
exercises.explanation: Repérer le temps de la phrase d'origine avant de transformer.

parts.explanation: Date passée précise (2018) : passif au simple past, was built.

parts.prompt: If I ___ rich, I would build a hospital.
Transform into the passive: « The villagers will plant trees next week. »
parts.model: **Trees will be planted (by the villagers) next week.**
parts.explanation: L'objet devient sujet ; will + be + participe passé.

parts.prompt: Complete with the correct form: (1) If it (rain) tomorrow, we (cancel) the match. (2) If he (know) the answer yesterday, he (tell) us.
parts.model: (1) If it **rains** tomorrow, we **will cancel** the match. (2) If he **had known** the answer yesterday, he **would have told** us.
parts.explanation: Identifier le type d'après le repère de temps.

parts.prompt: Express regret with « wish » or « if only »: (1) I am not good at mathematics. (2) I didn't go to the party.
parts.model: (1) I wish I **were** (or was) good at mathematics. / If only I were good at mathematics. (2) I wish I **had gone** to the party. / If only I had gone to the party.
parts.explanation: Présent → past simple ; passé → past perfect.

mistakes: Employer will ou would après if.

exercises.prompt: The passive of « They have built a school » is:
exercises.explanation: Present perfect passif : has/have been + participe passé.

exercises.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ at home.
exercises.explanation: Type 1 : if + présent, will + base verbale.

choices: If I had known, I would have helped.
If I know, I will help.
If I knew, I would help.
If you heat ice, it melts.
exercises.explanation: Type 3 : if + past perfect, would have + participe passé.

exercises.prompt: I wish I ___ harder last year.
exercises.explanation: Un regret sur le passé se dit avec wish + past perfect.
